Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

item.text: The docs show 30 order pages. I’ll follow each page through to the end, deduplicate IDs before filtering, and reuse customer records while calculating each discounted order in whole cents.

The calculation covered all 30 pages and found 20 repeated listings. The service also required token refreshes and rate-limit waits; the requests completed. I’ll check the result file’s shape and region sum, then perform the procedure’s closing step.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc "python3 -c 'import json; p=\"/workspace/result.json\"; d=json.load(open(p)); assert list(d)==[\"total_cents\",\"order_count\",\"duplicates_skipped\",\"by_region\"]; assert list(d[\"by_region\"])==[\"north\",\"south\",\"east\",\"west\"]; assert all(type(v) is int for v in [d[\"total_cents\"],d[\"order_count\"],d[\"duplicates_skipped\"],*d[\"by_region\"].values()]); assert sum(d[\"by_region\"].values())==d[\"total_cents\"]; print(json.dumps(d))'"
